The Road Code · Daily Lesson

Still On My Feet.

November 10, 2026 · Beaufort, South Carolina · Day 1,288 · 66,677.0 documented miles — this tour.

Still On My Feet — Part One, the film, 5:26

Seven days off the bike — a full week at the desk, finishing the book. Day 1,288, he rolled out of Walterboro pointed at Beaufort, and the first words on the road said it plain: “The book is done.”

Feels-like 39° at roll-out, riding fasted. Marsh water and long shadows first — then the highway took over, and the trucks with it.

The sun came up swinging; layers came off on the shoulder. Over the water on the Harriet Tubman Memorial Bridge, he called the next turn out loud: “Next up is Joe Frazier.” Then the trail took him in: “Thank God I’m off the highway. Thank God the gate’s open.”

Still On My Feet — Part Two: The Last Miles, 1:36

Mile 40, the leg went. “Wow! That would be a pulled muscle. Fantastic!” Twelve minutes later, at the stop sign: “Oh God, it hurt.” And in the same breath, riding away: “Joe Frazier — heavyweight champion of the world. Just like Coach.”

He rolled into Serenity Trails on one good leg. Wendy Heyward had the tent up and the welcome out — and told the Joe Frazier Road story to the camera herself. Dry-heaved at the end of the day: the tank was empty, and he was still on his feet.

The lesson — THE DISCIPLINE: The body votes no. The man outvotes it — finish on the leg you’ve got. A comeback isn’t proven by the miles that feel good; it’s proven at mile 40.

R.O.D.A. — Remain On Duty Always.

⚔️ Coach R.O.D.A. // The Road Code · Still On My Feet.
